---
title: Dashboards
description: Compliance-native operational views declared in YAML and rendered from the closed dashboard query catalog.
---

Dashboards answer **operational compliance** questions — open findings, remediation backlog, scanner activity, evidence gaps — for a workspace (and optionally one monitored process). They are file-backed config in your connected repository, not ad-hoc BI.

## File location

`.kiket/dashboards/*.yaml` — one file per dashboard. The Process Twin home surface loads `process-health` by default when present.

## Minimum dashboard

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: process-health
  name: Process health
  description: Open findings, remediation pipeline, scanner activity, and evidence gaps for this workspace.
  scope: workspace
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: open_findings_by_severity
    type: chart
    title: Open findings by severity
    query_key: platform.open_findings_by_severity
    config:
      chart: bar
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2 }
  - id: open_cases
    type: metric
    title: Open cases
    query_key: workspace.open_cases_count
    position: { x: 3, y: 0, w: 3, h: 1 }
```

## Widget types

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `metric` | Single number with optional tone |
| `chart` | Bar, line, area, or pie chart (`config.chart`) |
| `list` | Compact rows (findings, evidence gaps) with `config.limit` |
| `table` | Tabular rows with pagination limit |
| `text` | Static markdown-safe copy from `config.body` |
| `embed` | **Deferred in runtime v1** — validation fails until allowlisted embeds ship |

## Query catalog (closed)

Widgets bind to **`query_key`** values from a closed catalog — not free SQL or arbitrary JSONPath. Unknown keys fail editor validation and return errors from the batch executor.

| `query_key` | Typical widget types | Data |
|-------------|---------------------|------|
| `platform.open_findings_by_severity` | `metric`, `chart` | Unresolved findings by severity |
| `platform.findings_by_status` | `chart`, `table` | Findings grouped by triage status |
| `platform.remediation_pipeline` | `chart`, `list` | Remediation proof/completion pipeline |
| `platform.scanner_run_history` | `chart`, `table` | Findings observed per recent scanner run |
| `platform.findings_since_last_scan` | `list` | Findings first seen since last completed scan |
| `platform.latest_scanner_run` | `metric`, `text` | Most recent completed scanner run |
| `workspace.open_cases_count` | `metric` | Active operational cases (optional `processId` scope) |
| `workspace.evidence_gaps` | `list`, `table` | Open findings for missing required evidence |

List the catalog at runtime:

`GET /platform/dashboard-queries/catalog`

Execute one or more queries in a single round trip:

`POST /platform/dashboard-queries/execute`

```json
{
  "workspaceId": "<uuid>",
  "processId": "<uuid optional>",
  "queries": [
    { "queryKey": "platform.open_findings_by_severity" },
    { "queryKey": "workspace.evidence_gaps", "limit": 5 }
  ]
}
```

Resolve parsed YAML from a workspace-linked repository:

`GET /platform/dashboard-queries/workspaces/{workspaceId}/dashboards/{dashboardKey}`

## Runtime routes

| Surface | URL | Notes |
|---------|-----|-------|
| Process Twin (default) | `/` | Loads `process-health` from repo YAML or built-in default |
| Workspace dashboard | `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/dashboards/{dashboardKey}` | Deep-linkable generic runtime view |
| Visual editor | `/editor?file=.kiket/dashboards/{key}.yaml` | Layout + query picker + live preview when a workspace is selected |

## Create a new dashboard

In the visual editor, use **New → Dashboard** (or click the ghost `dashboards/` folder when empty). Kiket scaffolds `.kiket/dashboards/{your-key}.yaml` with workspace scope and one starter metric widget (`workspace.open_cases_count`). Add widgets in the editor, pick `query_key` values from the catalog, and use **Live preview** when a workspace is selected.

Validate dashboard YAML locally:

```bash
kiket validate --file .kiket/dashboards/process-health.yaml --local
```

## Scope

- **`scope: workspace`** (default) — aggregates across all monitored processes in the workspace.
- **`scope: process`** with `process_id` — restrict widgets to one monitored process when the dashboard is mounted in a process-specific shell.

## Layout

`layout.columns` defines the grid width (1–24). Each widget has `position: { x, y, w, h }` in column units. The editor visual canvas uses the same model.

## Examples

### Process health (flagship)

The default Process Twin surface loads `process-health` when the file exists in your connected repo. It binds all eight catalog queries across charts, metrics, and lists — see `definitions/engineering-change/.kiket/dashboards/process-health.yaml` in the definitions pack.

Open it at runtime:

`/workspaces/{workspaceId}/dashboards/process-health`

### Starter dashboard (editor scaffold)

**New → Dashboard** in the visual editor produces a minimal workspace dashboard with one metric widget:

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: team-ops
  name: Team operations overview
  description: Operational compliance dashboard for this workspace.
  scope: workspace
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: open_cases
    type: metric
    title: Open cases
    query_key: workspace.open_cases_count
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 1 }
```

Add widgets in the editor, pick `query_key` values from the catalog dropdown, and expand the grid from there.

### Findings triage focus

A narrower dashboard for daily triage — severity, status, and new findings since the last scan:

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: findings-triage
  name: Findings triage
  description: Severity mix, status pipeline, and deltas since the last completed scanner run.
  scope: workspace
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: severity
    type: chart
    title: Open findings by severity
    query_key: platform.open_findings_by_severity
    config:
      chart: bar
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 4, h: 2 }
  - id: status
    type: chart
    title: Finding status
    query_key: platform.findings_by_status
    config:
      chart: bar
    position: { x: 4, y: 0, w: 4, h: 2 }
  - id: since_scan
    type: list
    title: Findings since last scan
    query_key: platform.findings_since_last_scan
    config:
      limit: 8
    position: { x: 8, y: 0, w: 4, h: 2 }
```

Deep links on list rows open the Findings Inbox for the selected finding.

### Evidence gaps table

Use a `table` widget when reviewers need sortable rows instead of compact list cards:

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: evidence-review
  name: Evidence review
  scope: workspace
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: gaps_table
    type: table
    title: Evidence gaps
    query_key: workspace.evidence_gaps
    config:
      limit: 20
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 12, h: 3 }
```

### Process-scoped dashboard

Restrict all widgets to one monitored process by setting scope on the dashboard and passing `processId` when executing queries (the runtime API accepts an optional `processId` on `POST /platform/dashboard-queries/execute`):

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: change-approval-health
  name: Change approval health
  description: Health view for the production change approval process only.
  scope: process
  process_id: "<monitored-process-uuid>"
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: open_cases
    type: metric
    title: Open cases (process)
    query_key: workspace.open_cases_count
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 1 }
  - id: scanner_trend
    type: chart
    title: Scanner findings trend
    query_key: platform.scanner_run_history
    config:
      chart: line
    position: { x: 3, y: 0, w: 9, h: 2 }
```

Replace `process_id` with the UUID from **Processes** or `GET /platform/processes`. Process Twin remains workspace-wide; use this pattern when a dashboard is mounted in a process-specific shell.

### Scanner status strip

Combine a metric and static guidance text for operators watching scanner runs:

```yaml
dashboard:
  key: scanner-ops
  name: Scanner operations
  scope: workspace
layout:
  columns: 12
widgets:
  - id: last_run
    type: metric
    title: Last scanner run
    query_key: platform.latest_scanner_run
    position: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 4, h: 1 }
  - id: trend
    type: chart
    title: Findings per run
    query_key: platform.scanner_run_history
    config:
      chart: line
    position: { x: 4, y: 0, w: 8, h: 2 }
  - id: runbook
    type: text
    title: Runbook
    config:
      body: |
        Run a manual scanner pass after new evidence arrives.
        Triage new findings in the inbox before closing remediations.
    position: { x: 0, y: 1, w: 4, h: 2 }
```

`text` widgets do not bind a `query_key`; they render `config.body` as static copy.
